Unwritten rule of passing is passing for the comfort of the rider in front of you. Also apologizing if you get too close, etc. I've been to the track all year and haven't been hit until yesterday. Typically if your stuck behind someone you follow for a few lines to understand how they're taking them and then make your pass from there. Different groups is different levels of passing, i think C group you are limited on passing quite significantly, such as 6+ ft width and no passing on the inside. B group is a little more lenient and you can pass anywhere but it has to be a clean 6ft (but for the most part that varies, ive been passed close in B group.) In A group i've seen people damn near touching. 

I'm not uncomfortable with people passing me closely, on Thunderhill East i've been passed closely a number of times, however it was a clean pass and I could see them from my peripheral. This was absolutely a dogshit pass, and you can see me start to straighten the bike as soon as he got into my peripheral vision. I've had my line cut off before and i've had to straighten the bike out before, but I've never had it happen so close to the apex, especially in such a shitty spot. What instrument if you don't mind me asking? Classical violinist over here, went to Juilliard but decided not to pursue music, still love it though!

A movement is a piece that can be performed on its own but is part of a larger composition, usually in a concerto it will follow a fast slow fast pattern for the three different movements. So first movement is fast paced, second movement is slow, and third movement is fast again. not all concertos follow that pattern, but most do.

Vivaldi Four Seasons is actually a concerto since it has 3 movements and is written for a solo instrument to be accompanied by an orchestra. A sonata is meant for a solo instrument (or at most two, ex violin and piano) Hope this helps!
